description: getStatusColor()'s if/else both return unconditionally, so the console.log() statement after the if/else block can never execute under any input.

required_findings.justification: Both branches of the only if/else in this function return unconditionally, and the function has no loop or exception handling that could re-enter after a return — the console.log call after the if/else is unreachable under every possible input to `status`, which is a fully-typed two-value union. This is provable by control-flow inspection alone.

explanation: The clearest possible unreachable-code case: a statement placed after two unconditionally-returning branches. Severity capped at Nit/P2 since dead code, on its own, doesn't misbehave at runtime — it's a cleanliness/clarity issue (and here, mildly suspicious that a log statement was intended to run but the code was restructured around it), not a functional defect.
